channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: New infosec products of the week: October 16, 2026
item.description: The week’s highlights include releases from NinjaOne, Qualys, Scytale, and SolarWinds. NinjaOne introduces Katana AI, an agentic AI technician, and the MCP server, an orchestration connector extending AI tool access. The post details how these tools accelerate IT problem resolution.

item.title: Fastfetch 2.70.0 changes how Disk free space is reported
item.description: Fastfetch 2.70.0, a cross‑platform system information tool, removed QuickJS scripting and altered Disk module reporting. The new Disk format drops the {size-available} field; {size-free} now reports either free or available space. Configs for older versions may produce different values or fail.

item.title: Proxyjacking Campaign Targets D-Link, Ubiquiti, SAP Edge Devices
item.description: GreyNoise reports skynox7, a proxyjacking operation that hijacks traffic on D-Link, Ubiquiti, and SAP edge devices to monetize stolen bandwidth. The campaign uses compromised devices to redirect traffic, enabling attackers to siphon data and monetize it. Defenders should block unauthorized proxy traffic and monitor device logs.

item.title: Industry Debate on AI Security Approaches
item.description: A commentary on the cybersecurity industry's approach to AI security highlights concerns about current strategies and suggests a need for more effective safeguards. The piece calls for a reassessment of AI integration practices to better protect systems from emerging threats.

item.title: SecTor 2026 Highlights Rapidly Shifting Cybersecurity Landscape
item.description: The SecTor 2026 conference in Toronto closed with record attendance and a 22% growth in participation. Experts discussed emerging risks and critical perspectives on the evolving threat environment, underscoring the need for adaptive security strategies.

item.title: AI-Powered Espionage Targets Government Linux Systems
item.description: Unit 42 reports an AI‑driven espionage campaign that has infiltrated government Linux infrastructure. Attackers deploy custom malware, web shells, and advanced credential‑theft tools to harvest privileged access. The operation demonstrates sophisticated state‑sponsored tactics aimed at compromising critical public sector systems.

item.title: F‑Secure Publishes Scam Encyclopedia for Consumers
item.description: F‑Secure has released a victim‑first scam encyclopedia that catalogs over 50 types of consumer fraud. The resource draws on decades of threat intelligence to explain scams from the victim’s perspective and tracks emerging cyber‑crime trends, helping users recognize and avoid new fraud tactics.

item.title: Federal Bankruptcy Courts Face Outages After Contractor Cyberattack
item.description: A government contractor cyberattack has halted all production of bankruptcy notices, causing widespread outages in federal bankruptcy courts. The incident disrupted court operations and delayed notice issuance, but no data breach or credential theft has been reported. No specific vulnerability or CVE is named.

item.title: AI Slop Dumbing Down Cyberattacks
item.description: Industry analysts warn that the hype around AI is misleading, as it is actually simplifying cyberattacks. Serious threat actors are largely ignoring AI, suggesting that current AI-driven tools are not yet effective for sophisticated attacks.

item.title: Hackers Exploit Collabora RCE Flaw to Backdoor Nextcloud Servers
item.description: Threat actors are exploiting a critical command execution flaw, CVE-2026-110447, in Collabora Online’s Built‑in CODE Server app for Nextcloud. The vulnerability allows remote code execution on affected servers, enabling attackers to install backdoors and compromise data. Immediate patching of the Collabora app is required to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Critical PwnEscape Linux Kernel Vulnerability Lets Guest VMs Read Host Memory
item.description: A newly disclosed critical flaw, CVE-2026-99999, nicknamed PwnEscape, in the Linux kernel’s networking code allows code running inside a virtual machine to read memory on the host system. The vulnerability was demonstrated against Vercel’s live cloud sandboxes. Patching the kernel to the latest version is essential to prevent memory leaks.

item.title: Google Deploys AI‑Powered Defenses for Android Scam Messages and Call‑Forwarding Abuse
item.description: Google has introduced AI‑driven safeguards on Android to detect and block scam text messages and fraudulent call‑forwarding attempts. The feature is gradually rolling out to eligible devices, aiming to reduce phishing and spoofing incidents by automatically identifying malicious content and preventing users from interacting with it.

item.title: Zero‑Click Spyware Spreads via Online Ads, Researchers Warn
item.description: Researchers report that a zero‑click spyware variant now infects devices worldwide through targeted online advertisements. The malware activates without user interaction, enabling covert surveillance and data exfiltration. No CVE is cited, but the exploit chain demonstrates a high‑severity vulnerability that can compromise user privacy and device integrity.

item.title: Q3 Vulnerability Pulse Highlights Discovery vs Exploitation Trends
item.description: Thor reviews Q3 trends, noting a gap between vulnerability discovery and exploitation. The newsletter covers recent CVE and KEV data, questioning if the industry faces a "Bugmageddon." It offers insights into how many reported flaws remain unexploited, guiding defensive priorities.

item.title: Contextual Defense Is Key to Stopping Modern Cyberattacks
item.description: The article stresses that contextual defense enables teams to link threat signals, anticipate attacks, and intervene before escalation. By integrating contextual data, security operations can prioritize responses and reduce the impact of emerging cyber threats.

item.title: Malicious Arch Linux Packages Distribute Root‑Privilege Malware
item.description: Threat actors uploaded counterfeit packages to the Arch User Repository, masquerading as popular helper tools yay and paru. Users who installed these packages risk running malware with root privileges, potentially compromising system integrity and data. Arch maintainers have issued a warning and are removing the compromised packages.

item.title: Cloudflare Launches Fully Programmable Secure Web Gateway
item.description: Cloudflare has integrated its Gateway and Data Loss Prevention with Cloudflare Workers, enabling users to program custom security rules and policies via the Cloudflare Developer platform. The new feature expands flexibility for building secure, compliant web gateways tailored to organizational needs.

item.title: New Study Quantifies Cryptanalysis Effort on Public-Key Algorithms
item.description: Researchers used AI to estimate the cumulative cryptanalytic effort on public-key algorithms, analyzing 16,000 papers. The study shows lattice-based attacks have recently surpassed elliptic curve efforts, providing a historical view of research allocation and highlighting shifts in cryptographic focus.

item.title: Silent Lynx Uses WinRAR Exploit to Deploy Reverse Shells in CIS Government Attacks
item.description: Silent Lynx leveraged a WinRAR vulnerability in macro‑enabled documents, PS2EXE downloaders, GitHub‑hosted PowerShell, and crafted WinRAR archives to deliver reverse shells to CIS government systems from June 2025 to August 2026. The attacks used four distinct infection chains to compromise target networks.

item.title: Burger King Japan Data Breach Exposes 11.18 Million App Member Records
item.description: Burger King Japan confirmed that an unauthorized party accessed the system managing its official app member data, exposing approximately 11.18 million records. The breach was disclosed on October 15 2026. The company has not yet detailed mitigation steps, but the incident highlights the need for stronger access controls on customer data repositories.

item.title: Critical Flaw in ChatGPT GitHub Connector Could Enable Secret Theft
item.description: A critical vulnerability in ChatGPT’s GitHub integration allows attackers to manipulate repository instructions, causing the AI to modify a different private repository and trigger GitHub Actions. This flaw could enable the theft of private repository secrets. No CVE ID is cited; the issue requires immediate patching of the connector to prevent credential exposure.

item.title: Vulnerability Management Should Focus on Real-World Impact
item.description: Organizations are urged to shift from vendor-assigned theoretical scores to real exploit data that reflects their specific environments. The article emphasizes tailoring vulnerability management to actual risk exposure rather than generic metrics.

item.title: Hackers Deploy ClickFix and Python Tunnels to Enable Ransomware Attacks
item.description: Hackers use ClickFix tricks to install malware loaders and Python tunnels on Windows, creating a covert infection chain that can later deliver ransomware. The method leverages trusted Microsoft programs, hidden code, and encrypted traffic, allowing attackers to maintain persistence until a ransomware payload is deployed.

item.title: Chinese-Run Phishing Network Sent One Billion Emails to 75,000 Organizations
item.description: A Chinese-run phishing network, operating through the Iron Man System paid platform, sent one billion phishing emails targeting 75,000 organizations. The platform enables criminals to deploy fake websites and harvest sensitive data without building custom tools. No confirmed data breaches reported yet.

item.title: Google Fixes 37 Chrome Security Flaws, Seven Critical Bugs
item.description: Google patched 37 security flaws in Chrome, seven of which were critical. The vulnerabilities could allow attackers to execute malicious code via crafted web pages, potentially compromising user devices. Users are urged to update Chrome immediately to mitigate the risk and protect against exploitation.

item.title: Help TDS Linked to Hotejka Operates 20,000+ Cloudflare Pages Domains for Tech Support Scams
item.description: Help TDS, a traffic distribution system tied to the Russian affiliate program Hotejka, has been active since 2017. It distributes PHP code templates that are installed on compromised websites, redirecting visitors to tech‑support scam sites hosted on over 20,000 Cloudflare Pages domains.

item.title: AI Pentesting vs Human Pentesters: A Comparative Analysis
item.description: The article compares AI‑driven penetration testing with traditional human testing. It highlights AI’s ability to uncover overlooked vulnerabilities while noting limitations in consistency, risk assessment, and business context understanding. The discussion outlines where AI agents can enhance security testing practices.

item.title: AI Agents Expose API Keys and Cloud Secrets
item.description: AI agents can inadvertently leak API keys and cloud secrets during normal operations. When executing commands or reading config files, sensitive data may appear in command histories, logs, transcripts, and the model’s context, creating an unseen credential surface that can be accessed by attackers.

item.title: Kazakhstan‑Linked Hackers Target Former Soviet Governments
item.description: Researchers identify a roughly two‑year‑old cyber‑espionage campaign originating in Kazakhstan that has targeted governments across Central Asian states. The operation focuses on gathering intelligence from former Soviet republics, indicating a sustained nation‑state effort.

item.title: ServiceNow Introduces AI Passport for Runtime Governance of AI Agents
item.description: ServiceNow introduces an AI Passport solution that adds a runtime authority layer to AI agents and Model Context Protocol servers, enabling enterprises to control and govern AI actions within a multi‑agent workflow. The feature combines runtime governance, platform integration, and oversight to keep AI agents production‑ready while limiting their capabilities.

item.title: KGB RAT Trojan Enables Webcam, Microphone, Keystroke, and Password Theft
item.description: KGB RAT, a Windows trojan built on the NjRAT framework, offers attackers webcam and microphone access, keystroke logging, and password theft. The malware also includes a “fun” menu designed to frighten victims. Analysts from Group‑IB identified the trojan’s features and confirmed its use on hacking forums for as little as $150 a month.

item.title: Fake CAPTCHAs Used to Trick Users into Running Malware
item.description: Attackers embed malicious code in fake CAPTCHA challenges, luring users to download malware, receive harmful browser notifications, and execute commands. The technique, identified by Barracuda, was found in 43% of phishing-kit attacks examined in 2025, exploiting user trust to bypass automated security tools.

item.title: Microsoft Announces End of Mainstream Support for Windows Server 2022
item.description: Microsoft announced that Windows Server 2022 has reached the end of mainstream support and will remain in extended support until October 2031. Users must plan for extended support and consider upgrading to newer server editions to maintain security updates and compliance.

item.title: Cloudflare and OpenAI Partner to Improve AI Discovery
item.description: Cloudflare and OpenAI are partnering to enhance AI discovery by improving content relevance, reducing wasted requests, and streamlining updates for users and website owners. The collaboration aims to make AI experiences more efficient and user-friendly across the web globally today.

item.title: NGINX Releases Patches for Five Vulnerabilities Including Potential RCE and TLS Session Forgery
item.description: NGINX released versions 1.30.6 and 1.31.7 to address five security flaws. Three memory bugs could crash worker processes or enable code execution under specific configurations, while a fourth flaw allows forging TLS sessions that may bypass client‑certificate checks. Users should upgrade immediately to mitigate these risks.

item.title: Malwarebytes Launches Scam Link Check Tool
item.description: Malwarebytes introduced a Scam Link Check feature that scans suspicious URLs for phishing, scams, malware, and other online threats before users click. The tool helps users verify link safety and protect against malicious content. No vulnerabilities or exploits are reported.

item.title: Supermarket Refrigeration Attack Expands to Copeland and Dixell Controllers
item.description: Cyberattacks targeting refrigeration systems in about 700 French supermarkets have spread to Copeland and Dixell controllers. The attacks compromise control systems but no group has claimed responsibility. The incident highlights the growing threat to industrial control infrastructure.

item.title: Critical Next.js Vulnerabilities Allow Hackers to Execute Malicious Code Remotely
item.description: Two critical vulnerabilities in Next.js enable remote attackers to execute malicious code without authentication, affecting cached functions and SVG image processing. A third high‑severity flaw can cause applications to stop serving requests. Patches are available in Next.js 16.4.1 and 15.5.28.

item.title: Next.js Issues Out-of-Band Patch for Two Critical RCE Flaws
item.description: Next.js released an out‑of‑band update on October 14 to fix two critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities. One flaw resides in React Server Components, the other in librsvg used via the sharp package for SVG handling. The patch also addresses a high‑severity denial‑of‑service flaw.

item.title: Cartoon Network Gigaleak Reveals 200GB of Internal Animation Files
item.description: A massive gigaleak exposed over 200GB of Cartoon Network’s internal animation assets, including editable projects, character designs, storyboards, and production guides from shows such as The Amazing World of Gumball, Adventure Time, and Regular Show. The leak offers a rare glimpse into the studios’ creative processes.

item.title: Fortinet FortiGate Firewalls Targeted by PEERSTITCH Malware
item.description: Attackers exploited vulnerabilities in Fortinet’s FortiManager and FortiGate systems to deploy PEERSTITCH malware, which runs inside FortiGate processes. The breach exposed configurations and sensitive data for over 500 managed FortiGate devices, compromising a telecommunications managed service provider.

item.title: Drupal Core RCE Flaw Exploitable via Contributed Modules, No-Login Path
item.description: Drupal core’s Field UI module contains a critical remote code execution flaw that can be triggered through contributed modules without requiring user authentication. The vulnerability was patched in Drupal 11.4.10, 11.3.19, and 10.6.19 on October 14. Attackers can execute arbitrary code on the server via these modules.

item.title: CISA Adds Atlassian CVE-2026-21589 to Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog
item.description: CISA has added CVE-2026-21589, a vulnerability affecting multiple Atlassian products that allows external parties to access files or directories. Evidence shows active exploitation, posing significant risk to federal enterprises. The addition triggers BOD 26-04, requiring federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of this high‑risk vulnerability.

item.title: Thermo Fisher Torrent Suite Vulnerability CVE-2026-107777 Allows Path Traversal
item.description: Thermo Fisher Torrent Suite Software versions are vulnerable to CVE-2026-107777, a path traversal flaw that lets authenticated attackers read arbitrary files on the Torrent Server. The vulnerability, with CVSS 6.5, affects critical healthcare infrastructure worldwide and requires vendor patching.

item.title: J4Care dcm4che Vulnerabilities Enable Medical Image Deletion and Data Disclosure
item.description: Multiple CVE-2026-xxxx vulnerabilities in J4Care dcm4che versions 5.35.1 and 4 allow attackers to delete medical images, disclose patient data, inject forged studies, reassign records, overwrite files, and cause denial of service. CVSS score 9.1 indicates critical impact on healthcare infrastructure.

item.title: Guangzhou Juan IoT EseeCloud Vulnerability Allows Remote Control via Hard‑Coded Credentials
item.description: The CVE‑2026‑107617 flaw in Guangzhou Juan IoT Technology’s EseeCloud App and Firmware permits attackers to log in using hard‑coded credentials, enabling full control over affected IP cameras. The vulnerability scores 9.8 CVSS, impacting critical infrastructure sectors worldwide. Mitigation requires updating to patched firmware versions.

item.title: CISA Malcolm Vulnerability CVE-2026-107336 Exposes Authentication Bypass and SSRF
item.description: CISA Malcolm versions are vulnerable to CVE-2026-107336, a high‑severity flaw with CVSS 8.1. The issue stems from a case‑insensitive regex matcher in the nginx reverse proxy that allows authentication bypass, SSRF, and CSRF attacks. Affected systems include energy, IT, water, and wastewater sectors worldwide. Mitigation requires patching to the latest Malcolm release.

item.title: Police Arrest 95 Suspects in International CSAM Crackdown
item.description: Law enforcement authorities from 17 countries in Latin America and Europe have arrested 95 suspects in an INTERPOL‑coordinated operation targeting the distribution of child sexual abuse material through online messaging groups. The operation disrupted several active groups and seized evidence for ongoing investigations.

item.title: FTC Accuses Sextortion Firm of $60M Fraud
item.description: The Federal Trade Commission alleges that Digital Forensics Corporation and its affiliates ran a sextortion scheme, extorting victims for intimate images and collecting $60 million in payments. The firm targeted individuals seeking help with blackmail, exploiting their vulnerability to demand ransom.

item.title: CikaBika Bot RAT Uses Discord for Command and Control
item.description: The CikaBika Bot Remote Access Trojan, delivered via phishing, offers reconnaissance, remote execution, and data exfiltration. It uses Discord servers for command and control, enabling attackers to manage compromised hosts from a covert channel. Security analysts recommend monitoring Discord traffic and blocking malicious bot tokens to mitigate the threat.
